title: Optimizer Insights mini-card: inline batching & caching suggestions with quick-simulate
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a compact 'Optimizer Insights' mini-card that surfaces per-route batching and caching recommendations directly in the Per-Route dashboard and the rollout modal. The card should provide: a concise recommendation, an estimated cost delta, a confidence score, a 1-click 'Quick Apply' to set suggested config, and an interactive 'Simulate' slider that projects latency/cost change across a traffic profile. The goal is to reduce time-to-value for performance tuning and lower unit costs while preserving safety via guardrails.
background: Current console flows require engineers to navigate to the 'Optimize' workspace or read a long recommendation panel. That reduces adoption of batching/cache improvements. Several customers have asked for inline suggestions at the route level during rollouts so they can make fast trade-offs without context switching. This design explores a low-visual-weight card that can live in three places: per-route header, rollout configuration modal, and the quick insights rail on the left side of the dashboard.
goals: Surface actionable batching/caching recommendations without forcing a full workflow switch
Make expected cost/latency impacts immediately visible and understandable
Provide safe defaults and guardrails to prevent regressions
Enable a one-click apply path for engineers and a reversible rollout-based change path for platform teams
constraints: Must render within the existing Per-Route header (max width 360px)
Estimate calculations come from runtime service; UI uses up to 3s async fetch window
Quick Apply must create a rollout change, not bypass auditing for Private customers
Design must work for both hosted and Dedicated product tiers with minor permission differences
acceptance_criteria: Mini-card appears in Per-Route dashboard and rollout modal in Figma prototype
Simulate slider updates a compact micro-chart and numeric delta in the card
Quick Apply creates a draft rollout change and opens rollout modal for confirmation
Guardrail toggle warns when confidence < 60% or when estimated latency regresses > 15%
Unit tests cover UI state transitions for 'simulate', 'explain', and 'quick apply' interactions
prototype_notes: Prototype includes three states: collapsed (icon + summary), expanded (details + simulate), and rollout-confirmation
Simulate slider uses traffic distribution presets: p50, p70, p90 with an inline micro-chart showing latency vs cost
Explain button expands a short bullet list with the top 3 reasons the recommendation was generated (prefix caching candidate, KV hit-rate, batch-saturation)
user_research: 5 usability sessions with backend engineers (30-45m) on 2026-02-22 to 2026-02-25
Key finding: Engineers want a reversible quick path; they do NOT want silent changes to production
Key finding: Micro-chart triggered the right mental model; 2 participants asked for raw numbers tooltip
engineering_feedback: ENG-2984: runtime can provide an estimated token-cost delta and 95th latency projection, but rate-limits to 1/sec per route
ENG-3042: suggested Quick Apply should emit an audit event and create a rollout with canary by default
Performance note: compact card must lazy-load heavy chart data after initial render
review_comments: Jonah Kim (PM): prefer 'Quick Apply -> Draft Rollout' flow rather than immediate apply (security and audit)
Diego Martinez (SRE): add an 'observability link' that points to the route's trace view when confidence is low
Hannah Li (Design): reduce copy density in collapsed state; show only recommendation + delta
Liam O'Connor (Design): suggested subtle color-coding for confidence bands, accessible to colorblind users
decisions: Use rollout creation (not immediate apply) for Quick Apply to preserve audit and rollback behavior
Show confidence as a numeric percent and an accessible icon (low/med/high) rather than color alone
Cap the simulate slider range to recommended safe bounds to avoid encouraging extreme configurations
open_questions: Should promotions created by Quick Apply trigger an automated eval suite? (PM wants yes, ENG requests perf cost estimate)
What permission level is required for Quick Apply in Private deployments with stricter RBAC?
Do we show historical recommendation acceptance rate for this route to increase trust?
next_steps: Address ENG-2984 async rate-limit by adding a staleness indicator and cached value fallback (owner: ENG-2984)
Refine copy and micro-interactions per Hannah's notes and ship updated Figma by 2026-03-12 (owner: Sofia)
Create a small A/B usability test to compare mini-card vs full Optimize panel adoption (owner: UX Research)
Prepare an ops checklist for rollout-created changes to ensure canary windows and automatic rollback conditions
